# manimR

manimR is a native R port of [Manim
Community](https://www.manim.community/), the animation engine for
explanatory math videos. Scenes, mobjects, animations, LaTeX, text,
graphing, 3D and camera tools follow the Python API closely, so Manim
examples translate almost line by line. Rendering is done in R with
[grid](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/grid/html/00Index.html)
on an offscreen [ragg](https://ragg.r-lib.org/) device, and frames are
streamed to `ffmpeg`.

The website, <https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/>, has the full
reference and a set of articles that show every feature with rendered
videos:

- [Getting
  started](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/articles/manimR.html)
  and [Coming from Python
  manim](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/articles/coming-from-python.html)
- [Mobjects and
  geometry](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/articles/mobjects.html),
  [Animations](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/articles/animations.html),
  [Updaters and value
  trackers](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/articles/updaters.html)
- [Text, math and
  tables](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/articles/text-and-math.html),
  [Graphs, plots and coordinate
  systems](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/articles/graphing.html),
  [Cameras and 3D
  scenes](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/articles/cameras-and-3d.html),
  [Colors, images, SVG and point
  clouds](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/articles/colors-images.html)
- [Rendering, configuration and
  output](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/articles/rendering.html),
  [RStudio, knitr, Quarto and
  Shiny](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/articles/rstudio-knitr-shiny.html),
  [Math and utility
  functions](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/articles/utilities.html)

The introduction is also installed with the package:
[`vignette("manimR")`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/articles/manimR.md).

## Installation

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("adamrsophie/manimR")
```

System requirements:

- `ffmpeg` for video output (MP4, GIF, WebM, MOV).
- A LaTeX distribution with `dvisvgm` for
  [`Tex()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/tex.md) and
  [`MathTex()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/tex.md)
  (for example
  [`tinytex::install_tinytex()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/tinytex/man/install_tinytex.html)
  plus `tinytex::tlmgr_install("dvisvgm")`).
- Optionally the [typst](https://typst.app) command line compiler for
  [`Typst()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/typst.md)
  and
  [`MathTypst()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/typst.md);
  point to it with `manim_config(typst = "/path/to/typst")`.

Run
[`manim_check()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/manim_check.md)
to see what was found.

## A first scene

``` r

library(manimR)

SquareToCircle <- R6::R6Class("SquareToCircle", inherit = Scene,
  public = list(construct = function() {
    circle <- Circle()$set_fill(PINK, opacity = 0.5)
    square <- Square()$rotate(PI / 4)
    self$play(Create(square))
    self$play(Transform(square, circle))
    self$play(FadeOut(square))
  })
)

render(SquareToCircle, quality = "l", preview = TRUE)
```

The functional form is shorter for quick experiments:

``` r

render(function(self) {
  eq <- MathTex("e^{i\\pi}", "+", "1", "=", "0")
  self$play(Write(eq))
  self$play(Indicate(eq[3]))
}, quality = "l")
```

## Translating Manim code

| Python manim | manimR |
|----|----|
| `Circle(radius=2, color=RED)` | `Circle(radius = 2, color = RED)` |
| `sq.shift(LEFT).scale(2)` | `sq$shift(LEFT)$scale(2)` |
| `self.play(sq.animate.rotate(PI))` | `self$play(sq$animate$rotate(PI))` |
| `group[0]` | `group[1]` (indices start at 1) |
| `len(group)` | `length(group)` |
| `VGroup(*mobs)` | `VGroup(mobs)` or `VGroup(a, b, c)` |
| `t2c={"x": RED}` | `t2c = list(x = RED)` |
| `rate_func=smooth` | `rate_func = smooth_rate` or `rate_functions$smooth` (avoids masking [`stats::smooth()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/smooth.html)) |
| `rate_functions.ease_in_sine` | `rate_functions$ease_in_sine` (or `ease_in_sine`) |
| `from manim.utils.color import X11` | `X11_COLORS` or `color$X11` (avoids masking [`grDevices::X11()`](https://rdrr.io/r/grDevices/x11.html)) |
| `config.frame_height`, `frame.top` | `config$frame_height`, `manim_frame$top` (avoids masking [`graphics::frame()`](https://rdrr.io/r/graphics/frame.html)) |
| `with tempconfig({...}):` | `tempconfig(list(...), { ... })` |
| `ManimColor("#FF0000").darker()` | `ManimColor("#FF0000")$darker()` |
| `clip(a, 0, 1)` | `clip_value(a, 0, 1)` (avoids masking [`graphics::clip()`](https://rdrr.io/r/graphics/clip.html)) |
| `class S(Scene): def construct(self):` | `S <- R6::R6Class("S", inherit = Scene, public = list(construct = function() ...))` |
| `manim -pql file.py S` | `render_file("file.R", "S", quality = "l", preview = TRUE)` |

Every constructor `Foo()` has an exported R6 generator `FooClass` for
subclassing, for example
`R6::R6Class("MyShape", inherit = VMobjectClass, ...)`, including the
classes upstream defines only to preset arguments (`MathTableClass`,
`ReplacementTransformClass`, and so on). Constructors show the full
argument list of their class, so RStudio’s completion lists the same
arguments as Manim’s documentation. Class wide defaults work like
Manim’s
[`set_default()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/set_default.md):
`set_default(Text, font_size = 60)`.

Every public name of `from manim import *` has an R counterpart; the
only renames are the ones above, made so no export masks a base R
function (upstream’s [`choose()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/Special.html)
is [`base::choose()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/Special.html), and its
`unit` module’s members `Pixels`,
[`Percent()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/units.md),
`Degrees` and `Munits` are exported directly).
`tests/testthat/test-api-coverage.R` checks this against the upstream
source, for every exported name and every public method of every
exported class. Colors are hex strings;
[`ManimColor()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/ManimColor.md)
wraps one when you need upstream’s color methods. As upstream, a
misspelled argument (`Circle(raduis = 2)`) or setting
(`manim_config(qualty = "l")`) is an error.

Two exports share names with other packages:
[`Matrix()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/MatrixClass.md)
and `MatrixClass` (also in the Matrix package) and
[`Cross()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/geometry.md)
(also in purrr as
[`cross()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/space_ops.md),
a different case). Attach manimR last, or write
[`manimR::Matrix()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/MatrixClass.md).

## Rendering options

[`render()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/render.md)
and
[`manim_config()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/manim_config.md)
take Manim 0.22’s settings: `quality` (`"l"`, `"m"`, `"h"`, `"p"`,
`"k"`), `transparent`, `background_color`, `frame_rate`, `media_dir` and
the rest (see
[`?manim_config`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/manim_config.md)).
`format` chooses the artifact: `"auto"` (MP4, or MOV when transparent; a
scene with no animations is saved as its last frame), `"mp4"`, `"mov"`,
`"webm"`, `"gif"`, `"png"` (only the last frame;
`save_last_frame = TRUE` means the same), `"png-sequence"` (every frame)
or `"none"`; `dry_run = TRUE` renders without writing files. Output goes
to `media/videos/<module>/<quality>/<Scene>.mp4` and
`media/images/<module>/` like Manim; the media folder is in the R
session’s temporary directory unless you set `media_dir` (for example
`manim_config(media_dir = "media")`), while
[`manim_cli()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/manim_cli.md)
uses the R user cache folder (`--media_dir media` gives Manim’s
`./media`). The directory settings (`video_dir`, `images_dir`,
`partial_movie_dir`, `tex_dir`, …) take the same `{media_dir}`,
`{module_name}`, `{quality}` and `{scene_name}` placeholders
([`get_dir()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/get_dir.md)
resolves them). A `manim.cfg` file is read with
[`digest_config_file()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/digest_config_file.md),
and the command line reads one in the working directory.

Scenes can be split with `self$next_section("name")`; with
`save_sections = TRUE` each section is also written to its own video
under `sections/` with a JSON index, and
`next_section(skip_animations = TRUE)` skips a section while you work on
later ones. `self$add_sound()` and `self$play(..., subcaption = "...")`
add audio and an `.srt` subtitle file.

As in Manim, each play is written to its own partial movie file, named
by a hash of the renderer, the encoder settings, the camera, the
animations and the scene’s mobjects (including the values updaters use),
and the files are joined into the movie. Rendering again reuses the
files of unchanged plays; `disable_caching = TRUE` (`--disable_caching`)
renders everything, `flush_cache = TRUE` (`--flush_cache`) empties the
cache first, and `max_files_cached` (default 100) limits its size.
`video_codec`, `pixel_format` and `video_encoder_options` choose how the
segments are encoded.

`scene_frame(MyScene, t = 2.5)` renders the single frame at 2.5 seconds
without writing a video, and
[`plot()`](https://rdrr.io/r/graphics/plot.default.html) shows it.

From a terminal:

``` sh
Rscript -e 'manimR::manim_cli()' scenes.R SquareToCircle -ql -p
```

The command line takes all of `manim render`’s options (`-ql`, `-p`,
`-s`, `-t`, `-a`, `-o FILE`, `-n N,M`, `-r W,H`, `--fps`, `--format`,
`--save_sections`, `--dry_run`, `--media_dir`, `-c manim.cfg`,
`--encoder-option crf=18`, …) and the subcommands `checkhealth`,
`cfg show|write|export`, `init project|scene`, `plugins -l` and
`cache clear`; see
[`?manim_cli`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/manim_cli.md).

## RStudio

The package installs RStudio addins (Addins menu):

- **Render scene at cursor**: renders the scene defined at or above the
  cursor and plays it in the Viewer pane.
- **Render all scenes in file**.
- **Preview last frame**: renders only the final frame, which is much
  faster.
- **Insert scene template**.
- **Render scene in background**: renders as an RStudio background job
  and shows the result when it is done.
- **Render with options**: a dialog to choose scene, quality, format and
  transparency.

Set `options(manimR.addin_quality = "m")` to change the quality the
quick addins use. `plot(mobject)` draws any mobject in the Plots pane.

## Shiny

[`manimOutput()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/manimOutput.md)
and
[`renderManim()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/manimOutput.md)
show a scene in a Shiny app and render it again when the inputs it uses
change:

``` r

output$scene <- renderManim({
  n <- input$sides
  function(self) self$play(Create(RegularPolygon(n = n)))
})
```

## Other R graphics and data

[`as_mobject()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/as_mobject.md)
turns a ggplot2 chart, a grid grob or base graphics into a vector
mobject that can be animated, and `GraphClass$from_igraph()` builds a
[`Graph()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/GenericGraphClass.md)
from an igraph graph.

## R Markdown and Quarto

A `manim` knitr engine renders scenes inside documents:

```` markdown
```{manim, scene = "SquareToCircle", quality = "l"}
SquareToCircle <- R6::R6Class("SquareToCircle", inherit = Scene,
  public = list(construct = function() self$play(Create(Circle()))))
```
````

HTML output embeds the video, PDF output the last frame and other
formats (GitHub Markdown, Word) a GIF. The same engine works in Quarto
documents that use the knitr engine. In an `r` chunk, the value of
[`render()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/render.md)
is embedded the same way when it is printed.

## Differences from Python manim

- Scenes render with the Cairo style renderer (`CairoRenderer`), which
  draws with grid on a ragg device instead of pycairo, so the camera’s
  Cairo context helpers have no counterpart. With
  `manim_config(renderer = "opengl")`, scenes render with
  `OpenGLRenderer`, a port of upstream’s OpenGL renderer that draws in
  software instead of on the GPU: shader wrappers are drawn by a grid
  camera with the OpenGL camera’s projection and lighting (lit once per
  mobject, not per pixel), the projection shaders by their GLSL rules,
  and a live preview `Window` is an R graphics device. GLSL code of a
  `Mesh` is not run. The OpenGL point clouds (`DotCloud`, `TrueDot`,
  `OpenGLPMobject`) are drawn as round dots like upstream’s shader draws
  them, and the other OpenGL mobject classes (`OpenGLCircle`,
  `OpenGLSurface`, …) are subclasses of their Cairo counterparts.
- Interactive mode (`scene$interactive_embed()`,
  [`embed()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/embed.html), `interact()`) opens a
  Shiny window instead of upstream’s OpenGL window: it shows the live
  scene, takes the same key and mouse events (orbit, pan, zoom, `r`,
  `q`, `set_key_function()`) and has a code box in place of the IPython
  shell.
- Plugins are R packages whose `DESCRIPTION` sets
  `Config/manimR/plugin: true` (see
  [`get_plugins()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/get_plugins.md)),
  not Python entry points.
- [`Text()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/TextClass.md)
  uses system fonts through `textshaping` and `systemfonts` instead of
  Pango, so glyph shapes and metrics follow the installed fonts.
  [`MarkupText()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/MarkupText.md)
  wraps and justifies lines at upstream’s Pango layout width.
- Boolean operations
  ([`Union()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/boolean_ops.md),
  [`Intersection()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/boolean_ops.md),
  [`Difference()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/boolean_ops.md),
  [`Exclusion()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/boolean_ops.md))
  cut the input curves where they cross, as skia-pathops does, in double
  precision rather than skia’s single precision. A contour that holds no
  input start point can start at a different point, and an exclusion can
  split its outline into different (equally filled) contours.
- [`Code()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/CodeClass.md)
  highlights with Pygments, as upstream, when Python with the pygments
  module is installed; without it, a built in tokenizer highlights R and
  Python.
- Video segments are encoded in the R process, one at a time;
  `max_inflight_encoders` and `encoder_queue_size` are accepted but have
  no effect.
- Copy mobjects with `$copy()`; R6’s `$clone()` keeps the original’s id.
- [`ImplicitFunction()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/function_graphs.md)
  traces contours with
  [`grDevices::contourLines()`](https://rdrr.io/r/grDevices/contourLines.html)
  instead of an adaptive quadtree.
- Graph layouts, including `"planar"`, are native ports of the networkx
  algorithms, so igraph is not required. Where networkx picks an
  arbitrary element of a set, the first vertex is used, so a planar
  drawing can differ from networkx while staying free of crossings.
- In 3D scenes the camera’s `frame_center` is subtracted once (upstream
  subtracts it twice). Shaded strokes color each drawn segment from the
  shading gradient instead of filling a gradient, which looks the same
  at the thin strokes surfaces use.
- Images in formats other than PNG (JPEG, GIF, WebP and so on) are read
  through ffmpeg.
- Index valued helpers keep upstream’s 0 based numbers where they are
  arithmetic rather than positions in an R list:
  [`integer_interpolate()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/interpolate.md)
  and the `get_3d_vmob_*()` corner indices. Labels and positions that
  index R objects
  ([`index_labels()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/print_family.md),
  [`earclip_triangulation()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/earclip_triangulation.md))
  start at 1.
- [`subdivide_bezier()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/partial_bezier_points.md)
  splits curves of degree 4 or more at i/n, as its upstream
  documentation states; upstream’s code for those degrees splits
  elsewhere. Manim itself only uses cubic curves.
- [`override_animation()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/override_animation.md)
  and
  [`override_animate()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/reference/override_animation.md)
  replace the decorators of the same names:
  `override_animation(MyClass, "FadeIn", function(...) ...)`.
- `ZoomedScene` redraws the zoomed region as vector graphics instead of
  copying pixels.
- Arguments named `function` in Python are called `func` (a reserved
  word in R), and indices such as axis numbers start at 1.

## Fidelity tests

The test suite compares points, positions, colors, timings and LaTeX
output against reference data produced by Python manim (`data-raw/*.py`
regenerate the fixtures in `tests/testthat/fixtures/`). Geometry,
alignment, transforms, partial curves, rate functions, graphing, 3D
shapes, camera projections, graph layouts, matrices and tables match
upstream to within numerical precision.

## Acknowledgments

manimR is a port of [Manim
Community](https://github.com/ManimCommunity/manim), created by the
Manim Community developers on top of Grant Sanderson’s original manim
for 3Blue1Brown. Its design, algorithms and examples follow their work,
which is gratefully acknowledged. Manim Community is released under the
MIT license. The graph layouts are translated from
[NetworkX](https://networkx.org) (BSD 3 clause license) and the polygon
triangulation from [earcut.hpp](https://github.com/mapbox/earcut.hpp)
(ISC license).
